newsitem.title: GERMANY: German savings banks want tight money in 1997.
newsitem.headline: German savings banks want tight money in 1997.

text.p: Germany's association of savings banks called on the Bundesbank to set tight money supply growth targets for 1997 as this year's corridor of four to seven percent is likely to be overshot.

The association said in a statement it would be "appropriate" to set a tighter range on money supply growth next year. An expansion of between three and six percent would allow a balanced economic recovery to take place, it said.

On Germany's economic situation, the association said the economy grew again in the third quarter. But recovery had not yet become self-sustaining, was still dependent on exports and lacked support from domestic investment.
